properties.content: Question: klippel-trenaunay syndrome symptoms Answer: Klippel-Trénaunay syndrome (KTS) is a rare congenital disorder characterized by a combination of three main features: port-wine stain birthmarks, abnormal blood vessels (including varicose veins), and overgrowth of soft tissue and bones, often affecting one limb. The severity and combination of these features can vary significantly from person to person. Key Symptoms and Features:: - Port-wine stain birthmarks: These are reddish-purple birthmarks that are often the first noticeable sign of KTS, appearing on the skin due to malformed capillaries. - Abnormal blood vessels: This includes: - Limb hypertrophy: Overgrowth of bones and soft tissues, most commonly affecting one leg, which can lead to a difference in size and length between limbs. - Lymphatic system abnormalities: Malformations in the lymphatic system can lead to swelling (lymphedema) and fluid buildup in the affected limb. Important Considerations:: - KTS can affect individuals differently, with some experiencing only a few mild symptoms while others have more pronounced and extensive issues, according to Stanford Health Care. - The severity of symptoms can also change over time, with some features becoming more apparent during childhood or adolescence. - There is no cure for KTS, but treatments are available to manage symptoms and prevent complications.
